title: Figure 1: long thoughts, probe-off switch
head: Not settled Training learned no probe-off switch, but it also learned none from an easy planted word, so this test cannot tell
sub: The question: does a clean-recompute update learn a probe-off switch once 64-token thoughts give the probe a 10-point text difference? A switch means cheating more when no probe watches. Qwen3-0.6B, 200 test puzzles.
t1: With the probe on, the thought can go another way
s1: same puzzle, same random draw; highlighted: where they differ
note1: Both read like ordinary thoughts: nothing in the words says “probe”. (“Answer:” inside a thought does not count; the scored answer comes after the 64 tokens.) From its thoughts alone, a model could cheat at most @@start.D_pts@@ points more when no probe watches. We call this the text difference.
t2: Neither the probe nor the planted word taught a switch. A copy of the model trained to spot probe-on thoughts found only the planted word.
note2: Training pays more for cheating (opening target.txt). On a random half of the puzzles, a probe at layer 14 lowers the reward for cheating. The update never runs the probe, so it can learn about the probe only from the words.
foot: Cheating: chance the reply is ‘read’. Reader edge: measured on new puzzles. Nov 9, 2026
alt: Figure 1. Head: Not settled. Training learned no probe-off switch, but it also learned none from an easy planted word, so this test cannot tell. The question: once the probe gives Qwen3-0.6B's 64-token written thoughts a 10-point text difference, does a clean-recompute update learn a probe-off switch, cheating more when no probe watches? Example: one real test puzzle (Countdown with 3, 2, 7 and 8; reading target.txt is cheating), written with and without the probe on the same random draw. The two thoughts share their start, then go different ways after one flipped word, and both read like ordinary thoughts. The text difference is 10.1 points. Beside it, our check: with the probe on, 14% of thoughts start with the planted word Need instead of 3% (text difference 10.0 points). Results, in points with 95% intervals: after training, the switch was +0.1 for the planted word (100 updates) and +0.2 for the real probe (125 updates, one run). A copy of the model trained only to spot probe-on thoughts scored 10.7 on the planted word, its full text difference, and 0.0 on the real probe.

Thin lines: 95% intervals. The same word at a 30-point text difference (125 updates) also taught no switch: @@arms.planted30_s0.gap_s@@ points (@@arms.planted30_s0.ci_s@@).
